extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, peer reviewers, and researchers who evaluate or edit narrative (non-systematic) review articles (especially in medicine)
extracted.subtask_description: Use of the SANRA six-item scale to evaluate the methodological and reporting quality of narrative (non-systematic) review manuscripts; each item is rated 0 (low) to 2 (high) and summed (0–12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of the importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of the importance of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of SANRA's six items. Rated 0 (low standard) to 2 (high standard). The authors developed anchor definitions and examples to guide ratings. Raters in the study often disagreed on this item, suggesting it may need careful rater training and calibration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanation of the aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Explanation of the aims of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of SANRA's six items. Rate from 0 (low) to 2 (high). Anchor definitions and examples accompany the item in the full instrument to clarify expectations for what constitutes an adequate statement of aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literature search
rubrics_metrics.description: Description and appropriateness of the literature search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of SANRA's six items. Rated 0–2 with anchor definitions and examples. In the authors' testing this item showed a lower corrected item-total correlation (0.33), indicating more variability in how it relates to the overall scale; users should apply the search-related anchors consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality of referencing and presentation (how well sources are cited and presented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of SANRA's six items. Rated 0–2 with provided anchors/examples. Raters in the study often disagreed on this item, so explicit application of the anchor guidance and rater training is recommended to improve reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of evidence level
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of the level of evidence supporting statements (e.g., indicating strength/type of evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of SANRA's six items. Rated 0–2; anchor definitions and examples supplied in the instrument to help distinguish low vs high presentation of evidence level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of relevant endpoint data
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation of relevant endpoint data (reporting of outcomes/important data points relevant to the review topic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of SANRA's six items. Rated 0–2. In the authors' testing this item had the highest corrected item-total correlation (0.58), suggesting it aligns well with the overall scale; use the instrument's anchors/examples to judge adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring, implementation, and psychometric guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall scoring and recommended use of SANRA (scale structure, anchors, training, and psychometric properties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SANRA comprises six items each scored 0 (low standard) to 2 (high standard), producing a sum score from 0 to 12. The authors developed anchor definitions and examples for all items and recommend rater training based on the provided 'explanations and instructions' document. In a field test (30 manuscripts) SANRA showed feasibility in editorial work, internal consistency (Cronbach's alpha = 0.68), corrected item-total correlations ranging 0.33–0.58, and inter-rater reliability (ICC average measure = 0.77 [95% CI 0.57–0.88]). The authors removed an earlier item on writing and accessibility due to poor inter-rater reliability; SANRA is intended to complement journal-specific evaluation (audience, originality, difficulty) rather than replace editorial judgment. Further field testing, particularly of validity, was recommended.
